Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — sizing & cost-sensitivity

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and prefix caching options. We're mapping out committed capacity needs for H2 and want to lock a reserved pool, but we have a hard requirement: GPU market volatility.

Two asks from procurement:
- Can you provide 12/24/36-month sizing options tied to committed GPU-hours and an example pricing ladder?
- We need a clear protection mechanism (indexation, rebate, or adjustment window) if market GPU costs spike >15–20% over a quarter.

Elysium is open to a long-term commit but cannot carry full market upside risk for multi-year deals. If possible, include: a definition for the "GPU market index" you propose, a quarterly true-up process, and an example cap on pass-through.

Also: please attach a draft term sheet and a sample pricing table so procurement and finance can model sensitivity.

Can we aim to have a proposal by end-of-week?

Best,
Diana
Director, Procurement
Elysium.ai

Hi Diana — thanks, glad the demo was useful. High level options attached and a short proposal below. Draft term sheet attached (draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf).

Quick sizing/pricing options (illustrative):
- Option A (12-mo): 75k GPU-hours commit — list price $0.95 / GPU-hour — no index protection
- Option B (24-mo): 210k GPU-hours commit — base price $0.79 / GPU-hour — 8% standard discount
- Option C (36-mo): 420k GPU-hours commit — base price $0.71 / GPU-hour — 12% standard discount + reserved burst pool

Proposed cost-safety collar (new suggestion):
- GPU market index: weighted median spot+term GPU price from our market feed (Redwood GPU Index) on a quarterly cadence.
- Collar trigger: if index rises >15% QoQ, customer can elect either (a) rebate/credit applied to next invoice up to 10% of quarter committed spend, or (b) one-time adjustment window to reduce committed capacity by up to 15% with a pro-rated true-up.
- Upside cap: pass-through is limited to +25% of list GPU-hour rate; beyond that Redwood absorbs additional delta.

Discount mechanics: tiered by committed GPU-hours, negotiated on signing. Anything above 15% discount will require finance sign-off.

Attached: draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf — includes sample tables and a placeholder clause for the GPU Index. I'll loop in Finance for approvals if you'd like to see a higher concession.

Next steps: I can send a revised term sheet with the collar language formalized and a HubSpot deal link (RDW-5421) for your procurement team. Do you have a preferred DocuSign contact?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context, Grace. Finance reviewed the proposed collar and discount mechanics. Summary of finance position:

- Discount thresholds: Deal desk can approve up to 12% on 24-mo commits. Any discount >12% requires Director of Revenue Ops sign-off and >18% requires VP/GM sign-off. Document the margin impact in the HubSpot deal notes.

- Cost-safety collar: acceptable with conditions. Finance will accept a quarterly true-up + rebate model under these constraints:
  - Use Redwood GPU Index (our internal feed) as the official reference.
  - Trigger: index >20% QoQ triggers customer option for rebate (credit) or one-time capacity shrink with pro-rated refund.
  - Rebate cap: rebates may not exceed 8% of committed spend per triggered quarter; cumulative rebates across the term capped at 20% of total committed spend.
  - Pass-through cap: Finance prefers a +25% pass-through cap; beyond that Redwood assumes incremental delta to protect margin.

- Accounting/escrow: we can support a rebate escrow mechanism with quarterly reconciliation. Requires a short accounting playbook (I can draft).

- Approvals & conditions:
  - Approve 24-mo / 210k-hours @ 12% discount + collar per above, subject to Legal's standard T&C for capacity adjustments and SLA exceptions.
  - Any structural changes to the collar (higher rebate caps, higher discount) will require VP sign-off.

I've attached a one-page finance note that you can include in the HubSpot deal and share with the prospect (finance_approval_note.pdf). Please loop in Legal for final language.

Rachel Kim
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Diana — thanks for the patience. Summarizing agreed commercial terms and next steps below. This is a firm proposal pending your signature.

High-level deal (proposal):
- Account: Elysium.ai (RDW-5421)
- Commitment: 210,000 GPU-hours over 24 months
- Effective unit price: $0.79 / GPU-hour (list) — 12% applied discount on signing
- Upfront invoice structure: 9 monthly invoices (quarterly reconciliations) — details in attached term sheet

Cost-safety collar (finalized per Finance):
- Reference: Redwood GPU Index (internal feed) — quarterly measurement
- Trigger: index increases >20% QoQ
- Customer options on trigger: (1) rebate credit applied to next invoice up to 8% of that quarter's committed spend, OR (2) one-time capacity reduction up to 15% of remaining committed hours with pro-rated credit
- Rebate cap: 8% per triggered quarter; cumulative cap 20% of total committed spend across term
- Pass-through cap: +25% on list unit price; Redwood absorbs excess beyond the cap

Other commercial items:
- Legal: standard Redwood T&C plus a short rider for the collar mechanics and a single permitted adjustment during the term.
- Accounting: Redwood will manage rebate escrow and quarterly true-up; Rachel to share the playbook after countersignature.

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf, docusign_elysium_term.docx

Next steps:
1) If acceptable, please confirm by EOD 2026-05-28 and provide the DocuSign contact for signature.
2) Once signed, Finance will provision the rebate escrow and Ops will schedule capacity allocation.

Thanks — cc'ing Karthik/Tessa/Rachel to keep them on the loop.

Best,
